content.title: About
content.content: Cereal, O's, plain are dry, whole‑grain wheat flakes designed for a quick breakfast. The rings have a neutral flavor and a crunchy texture. They are typically poured with milk or a plant‑based drink and served immediately after preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: O's flakes first appeared in the 1970s as part of a "flat" breakfast line.
The product contains no added sugar, making it suitable for those monitoring sugar intake.
The original recipe uses only whole‑grain wheat, malt and salt.
Flakes dissolve quickly in hot milk but stay crunchy when cold milk is added.
Packaging often includes microwave preparation instructions.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: The flakes provide slowly digestible carbs that deliver steady energy throughout the morning.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain wheat supplies fiber that supports normal digestion.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Absence of added sugar makes the product suitable for people watching their glycemic load.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, riboflavin and niacin are present, supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Whole‑grain wheat provides a modest amount of iron, beneficial for blood formation.

items.title: Wheat/gluten allergy
items.content: The product contains gluten and may trigger reactions in individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic impact with sweeteners
items.content: Adding honey, syrup or other sweeteners can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar.

items.title: Potential mycotoxin contamination
items.content: Improper storage of grain can lead to mold and mycotoxin formation; observe best‑before dates.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour cold milk, kefir, plant‑based drink, or hot water over the flakes. They are often mixed into yogurt, smoothies, used as a base for granola, or incorporated into baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the flakes in the original package or an airtight container in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. For extended storage, place them in the refrigerator.

content.title: About
content.content: Cornmeal mush, no added fat is a cooked porridge made from cornmeal prepared only with water. It has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a smooth, creamy texture. The product is often used in infant nutrition and as a basic side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cornmeal is one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown by humans for over 7,000 years.
Fat‑free cornmeal mush is commonly served in schools and daycare centers as a low‑calorie carbohydrate source.
Unlike polenta, this mush is prepared without added butter or oil, making it low in calories.
Cornmeal is rich in iron and B‑vitamins, especially thiamine (B1).
Native American tribes traditionally prepared a similar porridge using stone grinding mills.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Cornmeal provides slowly digestible energy, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: The iron in cornmeal contributes to hemoglobin formation and supports immune function.

items.title: Contains vitamin B1
items.content: Thiamine is essential for proper nerve function and carbohydrate metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes this porridge suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Hypoallergenic
items.content: Cornmeal rarely triggers allergic reactions, making it safe for most people.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Cornmeal mush can raise blood sugar quickly, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Low protein content
items.content: Cornmeal provides little protein, so it should be paired with protein‑rich foods for a balanced meal.

items.title: Possible cross‑contamination with gluten
items.content: Processing facilities may also handle wheat, which is important for people with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the fat‑free cornmeal mush hot, optionally sweetened with fruit, berries, or a drizzle of honey. It can be used as a base for baby foods, as a side dish to meat, or incorporated into pureed soups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry cornmeal in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Refrigerate cooked mush and consume within 2–3 days, reheating before serving.

mixed-nuts-with-peanuts-lightly-salted.title: Mixed nuts with peanuts, lightly salted

content.title: About
content.content: Mixed nuts with peanuts is a blend of roasted nuts (almonds, cashews, hazelnuts, walnuts) and lightly salted peanuts. The nuts provide a crunchy texture and rich flavor, while the peanuts add a subtle sweetness and extra protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanuts are technically legumes, but they are treated as nuts in culinary contexts.
Mixed nut blends are popular in sports nutrition because they deliver protein and healthy fats in a convenient package.
A light touch of salt enhances the natural flavors without overwhelming them.
Varied nut sizes create an interesting mouthfeel contrast.
Portion‑controlled packets make mixed nuts a go‑to snack for on‑the‑go lifestyles.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Peanuts and most nuts provide a substantial amount of plant‑based protein that supports muscle repair.

items.title: Healthy monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats
items.content: The blend supplies heart‑friendly fats that can help maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Vitamins E and B
items.content: Mixed nuts are a source of vitamin E, a powerful antioxidant, as well as B‑vitamins such as B6 and folate that aid metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They contain magnesium, phosphorus, zinc, and iron, which are important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes digestive health and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Nut and peanut allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: The blend is calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Even a light salt coating adds sodium, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Large pieces can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the mix straight from the bag, sprinkle it over yogurt, oatmeal, salads, or incorporate it into baked goods. For extra aroma, you can briefly toast the nuts in a dry pan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the mix in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard any nuts that smell rancid.

pasta-with-tomato-based-sauce-meat-and-a.title: Pasta with Tomato-Based Sauce, Meat and Added Vegetables (Ready-to-Heat)

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with tomato-based sauce, meat and added vegetables is a ready‑to‑heat meal. It contains pasta, a tomato sauce, pieces of cooked meat (usually beef or chicken) and vegetables (carrot, bell pepper, onion). The dish provides a balanced mix of protein, carbohydrates and fiber, and is convenient for storage in the fridge or freezer.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tomato sauce is made from ripe tomatoes, tomato paste and aromatic herbs, making it a rich source of lycopene.
Meat is pre‑seared to retain juiciness and flavor.
Vegetables are diced finely, which speeds up cooking and boosts nutritional value.
The meal is popular as a quick lunch in offices and schools.
When stored properly in the freezer, the product keeps its taste for up to 6 months.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Meat and pasta supply essential amino acids needed for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Lycopene and antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes provide lycopene, which helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains vitamins B1, B3 and B6, supporting normal energy metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain pasta add fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Iron, zinc and potassium are present, contributing to immune function and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ready sauces can be high in salt; people monitoring blood pressure should watch portion size.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: If the pasta is wheat‑based, the product is not suitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some versions may contain food preservatives; those with sensitivities should choose preservative‑free options.

items.title: Overheating
items.content: Excessive heating can cause vegetables to become mushy and meat to dry out.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the meal in a microwave for 2–3 minutes (or follow package instructions), stir, and let stand for a minute. Serve as a standalone dish or top with a sprinkle of grated cheese and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0 °C to +4 °C for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 6 months. Ensure the packaging is intact before reheating.

pizza-with-extra-meat-and-extra-vegetabl.title: Pizza with extra meat and extra vegetables, thick crust

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with extra meat and extra vegetables on a thick crust is a hearty twist on the classic pizza, featuring an increased amount of protein and vegetable toppings. The dough is made from high‑grade flour, water, yeast, and olive oil, giving it a dense yet tender texture. A layer of tomato sauce is spread on the base, followed by generous mozzarella, a variety of meats (such as ham, sausage, chicken) and fresh vegetables (bell pepper, tomatoes, onion, mushrooms).

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thick crust holds more sauce and toppings, making each bite richer.
Extra meat boosts the protein content, making the pizza more suitable for an active lifestyle.
Vegetables retain most of their vitamins when added toward the end of baking.
Thick‑crust pizza traditionally comes from Naples, where it is known as “panzo”.
The combination of meat and vegetables balances salty and fresh flavors.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle repair and immune function.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Bell peppers, tomatoes, and mushrooms supply vitamin C, vitamin A, and potassium.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: The dough and cheese deliver complex carbs and fats for lasting satiety.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Mozzarella is a good source of calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables add fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Thick crust, cheese, and meat make the pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is advised for weight‑watchers.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and processed meats contain saturated fats that may raise cholesterol when consumed frequently.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Tomato sauce and cured meats are often high in salt, which can be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The pizza contains dairy and possible gluten traces, important for those with allergies or intolerances.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pizza hot, cut into individual slices. Fresh basil or arugula can be added after baking for extra aroma. Optionally sprinkle grated Parmesan or drizzle olive oil on top.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore a crisp crust. The pizza can be frozen for up to 2 months, wrapped tightly in plastic film and foil.

content.title: About
content.content: Coconut milk yogurt is a fermented beverage made from coconut cream. It has a creamy texture, mild tanginess, and a distinct coconut aroma. The product is vegan and suitable for those avoiding dairy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coconut milk contains medium‑chain triglycerides that are quickly metabolized for energy.
Coconut yogurt can be sweetened or left unsweetened depending on added ingredients.
Many coconut yogurts are fortified with probiotics to support gut health.
Unlike traditional yogurt, coconut yogurt contains no lactose.
Coconut yogurt can be used as a dairy‑free substitute for cream or sour cream in recipes.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Medium‑chain triglycerides in coconut milk may boost energy levels and support metabolism.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Added probiotics help maintain a balanced intestinal microbiome.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Suitable for people with lactose intolerance and those following a vegan diet.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Coconut milk provides vitamin E, an antioxidant that protects cells.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: The yogurt supplies magnesium and potassium, which support muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Coconut allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to coconut milk.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Coconut yogurt can be calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Coconut milk contains saturated fats; excess intake may be a concern for certain diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy it plain, add to smoothies, granola, fruit salads, or use as a base for dairy‑free sauces and dressings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the yogurt in the refrigerator at 2 °C–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days. Do not keep at room temperature.
